newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA, ROMANIA TO END DANUBE BRIDGE REPAIR IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA, ROMANIA TO END DANUBE BRIDGE REPAIR IN 1997.

text.p: Bulgaria and Romania will complete repair works on the only bridge linking them across the River Danube by May next year, Bulgarian transport officials said on Tuesday.

Hristo Saraivanov, chief of the transport ministry's investment department, told Reuters that the two-lane road bridge, which is under repair but still open to traffic, would be fully completed "next spring".
"Repair works are carried out simultaneously by the Bulgarian and the Romanian side, we are really working hard and we will lay the asphalt as soon as the cold winter is over," Saraivanov said.
The transport ministers of the two countries said in July the bridge would be repaired by October 31.

Repairs to the 40-year-old bridge linking the Bulgarian river port of Rousse and the Romanian town of Giurgiu, are expected to cost more than one million Ecus. The European Union's Phare programme will cover more than half the cost.
There are also three ferry links on the river between the two countries. They are Vidin - Calafat, Rousse - Giurgiu and Oryahovo - Becket.
A further ferry between the Bulgarian port of Silistra and the Romanian town of Calarasi is now under construction.

Saraivanov said a tender would be called by the end of the year for the construction of a parking space at the Rousse ferry port, the reconstruction of a quay and deepening of the waterway to the ferry port.
Bulgaria will open a new road linking the town of Vidin with the ferry pier on October 22.
The 2.7-km stretch has cost some 1.4 million Ecus and was built with the help of the European Union's Phare programme.
Bulgaria and Romania have failed so far to solve their dispute on the location of a new Danube river bridge.
